location: US Corn Belt (Iowa, Indiana, Missouri, Ohio, Illinois, Michigan), USA
comparison: fields cover cropped >=3 years (2015-2020) vs. fields never cover cropped
quote: The causal forest results indicated that fields where cover crops were adopted for 3 or more years experienced an average maize yield loss of 5.5% (95% confidence interval [CI]: 5.1–­5.9) in the study region, compared with fields that did not practice cover cropping.
note: Loss, i.e. effect = -5.5%. Log-yield model; yields from satellite (SCYM) for 2019-2020.

location: US Corn Belt (Iowa, Indiana, Missouri, Ohio, Illinois, Michigan), USA
comparison: fields cover cropped >=3 years (2015-2020) vs. fields never cover cropped
quote: On average, soybean yields were reduced by 3.5% (95% CI: 3.2–­3.9) following cover crop adoption, with 2.6% of CATEs having a positive value (Figure 7).
note: Reduction, i.e. effect = -3.5%. Same 3.5% when using yield levels instead of log yields.

comparison: fields cover cropped >=3 years vs. never cover cropped; yield levels model (robustness check)
quote: For maize, the mean effect when using levels was a yield loss of 5.2% compared with 5.5% for logs, while for soybean the mean effect was 3.5% for both.
note: Robustness check; not the headline estimate.

comparison: placebo test: future cover crop treatment status vs. mean 2000-2010 maize yields (before adoption)
quote: For the placebo test based on mean 2000–­2010 maize yields, the estimated treatment effect was not significantly different from zero (average treatment effect  =  −0.4%; 95% CI: −0.9–­0.1).
note: Placebo/selection-bias check, not a cover crop yield effect; value uses Unicode minus as printed.
